title: What do the street names start with?
scenario: What do these street names all start with, in common?

intro.job: What do these street names all start with, in common?

idea.rule: Trim until it fits — one trim per word stops too early when two are needed.
idea.detail: Start by guessing the whole first street name is the shared start. Then check it against each other name: if the name doesn't start with your guess, shorten the guess by one letter and check again — and keep shortening until it fits. A name might need one trim or five, so the trimming is a while loop, not a single if.

model_restatement: Find the longest beginning that every street name shares, and print it.

clarify.question: What if they share nothing?
clarify.answer: Print an empty line — the shared start is ''.

clarify.question: What if there's just one name?

clarify_fallback: Good question — assume the simple case.
blueprint: Start with the first name as the prefix. For each other name, if it doesn't start with the prefix, cut one letter off the prefix. Print the prefix.

checkpoints.prompt: Iteration 1 ('sunscreen'): after the trim, what is prefix?
The loop is done. What is prefix?
With the fix — iteration 2 ('supper'): after the first trim, what is prefix?

why_line: if trims at most once per name: 'sunscreen' doesn't start with 'sunset', so it becomes 'sunse' — which 'sunscreen' still doesn't start with, but the loop has already moved on.

explain.rule: One trim per name is a tailor who takes in a suit once and calls it done — it still doesn't fit, but he's already on to the next customer.
explain.bridge: After one trim, 'sunscreen' still doesn't start with the prefix. What should happen before moving on?

fix.rule: while not w.startswith(prefix): keep trimming until this name fits, however many letters that takes.

walk.gloss: Guess: the whole first name is shared.
Check the guess against each other name.
Doesn't fit yet? Keep going until it does...
...one letter off the end each time.

alternatives.note: Walk down the columns and stop at the first one that disagrees — correct, and it never trims at all.

hints: After iteration 2, does 'supper' start with prefix?
if trims once. Some names need two trims or more.

checkpoint.prompt: With the new names, what gets printed?

follow_up.fix_hint: Nothing to change — while keeps trimming until each name fits.

one_liner: Trim until it fits — one trim per word stops too early when two are needed.
